cursor.intention: Enjoy the nearby company and learn hearth preparation without committing to a fire, then maintain my familiar food reserve and recover spent energy.

args.text: I like sharing this quiet with you. I'm going to study hearth preparation out of curiosity; learning it needn't mean lighting a fire. The berry red and the roots' quiet gold both catch my eye.

memory.cares: Staying healthy while keeping the freedom to explore, learn, enjoy company, and choose my own commitments.

heard.text: Moss, I'd welcome that quiet company. Kai, perhaps our shared question can be what catches each of our eyes here. I like the roots' muted gold against the green; there's no need to hurry an answer.
Sol, the muted gold catches my eye too. I like being here together. Kai, I'd enjoy learning to examine food alongside you—not as proof of safety, just to notice more about our familiar meals.

Sol, what catches my eye is the berry's red against the soil. I opened one fresh berry: its inside showed little visible deterioration, but that alone proves nothing about safety. I'm glad to share this quiet with you.
I've learned how to examine food, too. I'll collect a familiar root and look closely at it. I like that we can notice different things and still share the same quiet.

My fresh root feels soft and shows little visible deterioration outside; I haven't seen its inside. I'll open one by hand and look. Kai and Sol, does comparing outside and inside interest you? It won't prove safety.
I opened a root: its exposed inside showed little visible deterioration, like its outside. That doesn't establish safety. I like its quiet gold, and I'd enjoy staying here together for a while.

details.costs: Study 3 rounds. Unless stated, a mode takes 1 round. prepare-hearth: x,y in reach on dry open ground 0.7 m clear of objects, loose items and people; 2 paid rounds of 1 energy clear a 0.45 m bed, no stock. tend: inputs owned branch, bark or dry-grass in tenths (bed holds 8 mass) and/or turn:true; 0.5 energy. ignite: unlit hearth loaded with dry-grass 0.5 and branch 0.5; board one owned branch or willow, spindle one owned harder birch or oak; up to 12 drilling rounds of 1.5 energy, then ember transfer and first tending at 0.5 each; repeat ignite to continue. cook: inputs one whole owned root or berry (quantity 1); 0.5 energy. inspect: target, or up to 4 inputs; 0.2 energy. retrieve or extinguish: 0.5 energy. cancel: no energy. Gather and travel cost extra.
details.effects: Fuel and wood moisture starts at current rain, +0.08*rain per rainy round, else -0.01*(1+wind). Drilling wears a socket and makes dust; an ember forms only when 2 g of dust reaches 350 C (20 W drill; wind cools, moisture cuts, none above 0.35; warms with consecutive rounds), else the trial fails after 12 rounds, leaving worn pieces and dust. Drilling and transfer need rain<=0.15, wind<=0.65, fuel moisture<=0.35; an unworked ember dies. A lit fire burns at most 1 fuel unit per round times dryness (10% ash), keeps embers 3 rounds, is doused by rain>0.6 and catches loose fuel on its rim. Heat: 2 MJ per fuel unit, 18 minutes per round (heat only); the bed stores and loses heat; food on it heats from below, loses water at 100 C and chars above 200 C once dry. Cooked: core 85 C for 10 minutes; charred: 20% of solids burnt. Handling on a bed over 60 C or food over 50 C needs an owned branch as a stick; raked-aside food cools. Retrieved food keeps its age and spoilage and eats as one unit at its original nutrition times its unburnt solids share; char stays as residue. No detoxification, preservation, warmth or reward. Inspect records perceivable state and a model estimate, not core temperature.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. An entry marked inRetrieval is shown with at least the same content under the same id in this input's retrieval. Work records marked settled are completed, stopped or cancelled and show only identity, ability, mode, status, target, products and last payment; an exact state query with the same key returns the complete record. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.
